title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: One past occurrence of competitor entry (not quantified), but recent price hike at same level (12.03) saw sales drop to x0.69 vs baseline (13 units). Noise-adjusted effect for new demand-eroding events is shrunk toward 1.0; evidence suggests ~25% downside.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. The product's price is raised 6.2% to $12.03, above regular $11.33. Past promotions show a median lift of x1.52, but the noise-adjusted estimate is only x1.4. The current week has no promotion, but a competitor opens across the street—this is a known demand-eroding event. The recent price increase (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) had no promotion, yet sales were 13 and 24 units (vs baseline 18.7), suggesting a price sensitivity effect. The 2026-09-28 week, at same price, sold 13 units (x0.69 vs baseline), indicating a downside effect. The competitor entry is a new, non-promotional, demand-reducing driver. Evidence is limited to one past event (competitor entry), so shrink effect toward 1.0. Use x0.75 as a conservative, noise-adjusted estimate for the competitor effect. No other drivers. No uplift from classical model. Combine: x1.0 × x0.75 = x0.75. Spread increases slightly due to uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 3.6 - 38.4 | 10%-90%: 7.5 - 34.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
